Summary:
1. Upstream inventory, from a scanner over `_ref`: 300 `.rs` files, 190,679 LOC, 6,706 public items (3,099 of them macro-generated `Styled` methods), 869 tests, 47 examples.
2. `PARITY.md` holds totals, naming rules N1-N14, file rules F1-F6, the 300-file map, the deviation registry, examples and external ports; item and test rows live in `parity/<area>.md` so parallel stages never edit the same file.
3. Every row has a rule-derived Go symbol and status `todo` (`gpui_tokio` rows are `n/a:D-TOKIO`); all 4,445 row line numbers were checked against source, and every `path:line` in both docs was range-checked.
4. Layout: root `gpui` holds the whole core crate; leaves are `collections`, `gpuiutil`, `refineable`, `sumtree`, `scheduler`, `a11y`, `internal/{taffy,etagere,lyon,jsonschema}`; back ends are `platform/*`, `render` + `render/wgpu`, `text/gotext`, `examples/*`.
5. Boundaries: cgo enters only through `render/wgpu` (and the wlspike dev tool); shared OS bindings live under repo-root `internal/{linux,apple,win}`; platforms use purego; `runtime.LockOSThread` sits in `platform`'s `init`; the root package has a single writing lane.
6. API decisions: generic methods on concrete types, `Element[RL, PP]` behind a typed `drawable`, and self-typed mixins (`Styled[S]`, `Interactive[S]`, `Parent[S]`) for fluent chaining.
7. Drop semantics: explicit `Release`/`Cancel`/`Unsubscribe`, `weak` handles, and `runtime.AddCleanup` as safety net; the leak detector is ported 1:1.
8. Async: tasks are `iter.Pull` coroutines with `task.Await(cx) (T, error)`, on one scheduler for tests and production with seeded PCG.
9. Re-expressed idioms each carry a deviation id (20 in total, D-NAME through D-MACRO); section 5.8 lists what stays 1:1 (effect queue, entity map, window phases, key dispatch, style cascade, scene, text layout, elements, test scheduler, shaders).
10. Codegen is in-repo `go:generate` tools: `stylegen`, `refinegen`, `actiongen`, `wlgen`, plus `paritycheck` for CI.
11. Stage plan: 129 stages in STAGES.md across three builders; M0-bootstrap creates the repo files and CI, M0-contracts lands the shared contracts and stubs so later stages run in parallel; the root package is one serial lane.
12. Milestones follow M0-M4; M1 exit is the `hello_world` window and quads on Hyprland, and its text only appears at M2 exit.
13. The language-level API shapes were compile-checked on go1.27.4 in scratch programs (mixins, generic methods, `iter.Pull` under `LockOSThread`, `weak`, `AddCleanup`, `encoding/json/v2`); nothing of the port itself is built yet.
14. Parity limits are L-GLYPH, L-JPEG, L-SVGTEXT, L-WGPUVER and L-WEBTHREADS; risks and their containment are in section 12.
15. Owner decisions (section 14) are all decided: libwayland-client via purego with wlgen wrappers, godbus/dbus/v5 v5.2.4, the WebGL2 fallback ported (L-WGPUVER, L-WEBTHREADS accepted), internal/jsonschema, and screen capture ported on Linux, Windows and macOS.

Parity bookkeeping: each stage edits only the area files in its owns list, row by row (never rewrite a whole file), in the same change as the code. Status is `todo`, `done`, `dev:<id>`, `n/a:<id>` or `blocked:<stage name>` (a test or item that needs a later stage). `blocked:owner` is not used: every item is ported, and what only a person can confirm (a device, a browser, an interactive dialog) is an owner check (decision 30) while the row is `done`. A row that uses an accepted limit cites it as `dev:L-<x>` (behaviour differs) or `n/a:L-<x>` (the item cannot exist). New deviation ids are registered in a `## Deviations registered here` table at the end of the stage's own area file, not in PARITY.md. Items the scan missed get new rows. `go run ./internal/cmd/paritycheck -area <a> [-done <upstream prefix>,...] [-all-done [-allow-blocked]] [-lint] [-rescan]` must pass before a stage is finished; `-allow-blocked` tolerates `blocked:<stage>` only while that stage has no docs/port/status/<stage>.done. External ports get docs/port/parity/ext-<name>.md created by their first stage.

AGENT.md, TECH_DEBT.md, docs/port/PARITY.md, docs/port/OWNER-CHECKS.md and .github/workflows/ci.yml are edited only by M0-bootstrap and the exit and CI stages. Every other stage writes hacks and known issues to docs/port/debt/<stage>.md at the moment it writes them, handoffs to docs/port/handoff/<stage>.md, owner checks to docs/port/owner-checks/<stage>.md, and on completion creates docs/port/status/<stage>.done with its verify result (one file per stage in shared directories, so there are no edit conflicts).

Go API shape (DESIGN 5-6): generic methods on concrete types (`Entity[T].Update`, `App.New`, `Context[T].Subscribe`); a generic method cannot be part of an interface, so AppContext is sealed with unexported non-generic primitives and the generic operations are free functions over it (`gpui.AppContextNew`, `AppContextReadGlobal`, ...) plus same-named generic methods on each concrete context type (DESIGN 6.2); closures returning a value use the `R` suffix (`Update` / `UpdateR`); `anyhow::Result<T>` -> `(T, error)` and upstream's `VisualContext::Result<T>` -> `error` / `(R, error)` (`UpdateIn`, `UpdateInR`), panics stay panics; returned `Option<T>` -> `(T, bool)` or a nil-able type, Option struct fields -> `gpui.Option[T]` (alias of gpuiutil.Option); iterators -> iter.Seq / iter.Seq2, `impl IntoIterator` parameters -> slices or variadics; field-less enums -> `type X uint8` with `XVariant` constants, data enums -> sealed interfaces or comparable tagged structs; `impl Into<X>` -> the concrete type, a sealed `IntoX` interface, or a union-constrained generic; TypeId -> reflect.Type; `gpui.Task[T]` is an alias of scheduler.Task[T].

Elements: `Element[RL, PP]` with typed state behind an unexported drawable, never `any`; optional hooks are separate interfaces the drawable type-asserts (`ElementA11y`, `ElementA11ySyntheticChildren[PP]`). Fluent traits are self-typed mixins embedded in each element (`Styled[S]`, `Interactive[S]`, `StatefulInteractive[S]`, `Parent[S]`, `Fluent[S]`) and bound in the element's constructor with the helpers documented in docs/api-contracts.md; chains keep the concrete type (`NewDiv().Flex().SizeFull()` is `*Div`). `Stateful[E]` is IntoElement-only and delegates to its inner element (DESIGN 6.5). SharedString implements IntoElement; plain strings go through `Parent.ChildText`. No element type may declare a method whose name is in docs/port/parity/styled-methods.tsv or the interactive method sets. `Element::id` is `ElementID`, constructors that collide with a type are `New<Type>`.

Handles and Drop (D-RAII): a handle value aliases one counted handle; `Clone()` makes a new one, `Release()` is the explicit drop (idempotent, use after release panics). Every upstream `impl Drop` has a row in the Drop table of DESIGN 5.2 naming its Go method (Release, Close, Destroy, End, Cancel, Unsubscribe) and when it runs; ported code calls it exactly where upstream drops, moves into `detach()`, or lets a value go out of scope, usually with `defer`. The App borrow guard (AppCell, DESIGN 5.2) panics on re-entrant mutable borrows with upstream's message. Subscriptions and tasks never stop because of garbage collection; runtime.AddCleanup is only the safety net for entity and focus handles and the leak reporter. Tests in this repo run with strict leak detection.

Async (D-ASYNC): tasks are iter.Pull coroutines scheduled by the scheduler package in tests and production; `.await` is `task.Await(cx)`; a foreground task holds `*AsyncApp`, not `*App`, and blocks only in gpui / scheduler primitives (Await, Timer, Chan, Oneshot, Select, Yield), never on a raw channel, mutex wait or time.Sleep. iter.Pull's next and stop must not run concurrently or re-entrantly, so `Cancel` only sets an atomic flag and wakes the task; the poll loop that owns the coroutine calls stop() on its next poll (DESIGN 5.6). Test randomness comes from the scheduler's seeded PCG (D-RNG).

Actions: an action type implements `Name`, `BoxedClone`, `PartialEq` and registers itself with `gpui.RegisterAction` from `init` (by hand or with `//gpui:action`, actiongen). JSON goes through encoding/json/v2 (`encoding/json/v2`, `encoding/json/jsontext`) everywhere in the port; schemas through internal/jsonschema.

Tests: every upstream test is one Go test named by rule N14 (`TestKeymap_Foo`, inner module name after the file stem), in `<file>_test.go` of the same package; `#[gpui::test]` bodies run inside `gpui.RunTest` with upstream's seeds / iterations / retries; `#[ignore]` becomes t.Skip with upstream's reason; cfg(target_os) gates become build constraints; benches become `Benchmark<File>_<Name>` on gpui.RunBench. Fix the code, not the test, when a ported test fails. Test support (TestAppContext, TestPlatform) lives in ordinary files of the root package.

Test isolation on the developer's machine: `go test` never opens a window, never talks to the session bus, the a11y bus, the keyring, the notification daemon or the system clipboard, and never starts or stops user services. Tests that need a display run only with GPUI_TEST_DISPLAY=1; D-Bus tests use a fake connection or a private dbus-daemon started by the test, and programs that need a bus run under `dbus-run-session --`; credential tests use unique names and delete only what they created; GPU tests skip when no adapter is found.

Generated code is committed, named `*_gen.go` (or the tool's documented data files), starts with `// Code generated by <tool>; DO NOT EDIT.`, and is produced by a `//go:generate go run github.com/megascan/gpui-go/internal/cmd/<tool> ...` line in a hand-written file of the same package; `go generate ./...` must leave every generated file byte-identical (verify with checksums, not `git diff`: the tree is not committed between stages). Tools that wrap an external program (metalhdr: cbindgen, glslgen: naga) exit 0 with a message when it is missing, so the committed output is used. Directives are `//gpui:refineable` and `//gpui:action`.

Build rules: the root package imports no platform, renderer, cgo or purego code (DESIGN section 4 import rules, enforced by `paritycheck -lint`). cgo is allowed only in render/wgpu (constrained to `linux || js`) and in the dev tool internal/cmd/wlspike. internal/linux/** is `linux`, internal/apple/** `darwin`, internal/win/** `windows`, and only packages with the same constraint import them. Linux packages are `linux`, Apple packages `darwin` (macos: `darwin && !ios`, ios: `ios`), platform/windows `windows`, platform/web `js && wasm`. Everything except render/wgpu's cgo files must pass `CGO_ENABLED=0 go vet` and `go test -c -o /dev/null` for darwin, windows and js/wasm from Linux (ios: vet only, it needs external linking). `runtime.LockOSThread()` is called in `init` of package platform only; the root package never locks a thread. File stems never end in a GOOS / GOARCH word by accident (F3).

Seams between packages: render/render.go (the `Renderer` interface, created by M0-scene) is what platform windows hold; Linux constructs it with `wgpu.NewRenderer`, macOS and Windows with their own renderers. render/wgpu is written against its GPU facade render/wgpu/internal/gpu, implemented by internal/gpu/webgpu (native and browser WebGPU) and internal/gpu/webgl2 (the browser fallback). All atlases use internal/etagere. The Linux and web text system is text/gotext (`NewTextSystem`, `NewTextSystemWithoutSystemFonts`). Screen capture: the root declares `ScapBackend` and `RegisterScapBackend` (M0-platform-types) and ports upstream's scap glue on it (M3-root-capture); the Linux back end registers from platform/linux, the Windows one from platform/platform_windows.go; macOS uses its own ScreenCaptureKit path as upstream does. Conversions between gpui types and internal/taffy, internal/etagere or internal/lyon types live in the bridge files (taffy.go, path_builder.go, the atlas implementations), never in geometry.go, style.go or platform.go. Each platform window package has an `a11y.go` seam that the adapter stages fill.

GPU data: scene primitive structs keep upstream field order with fixed-size 4-byte-aligned fields and are uploaded with unsafe.Slice; scene_layout_test.go pins sizes and offsets. Shader files (4 WGSL, shaders.metal, shaders.hlsl, alpha_correction.hlsl) are byte-identical copies embedded with //go:embed and checked by sha256 against `_ref`. Metal compiles the cbindgen scene.h header (internal/cmd/metalhdr, cbindgen 0.28.0, as gpui_apple/build.rs) followed by shaders.metal, as upstream's runtime_shaders path does; HLSL's `#include "alpha_correction.hlsl"` is served by an ID3DInclude handler; the WebGL2 path uses GLSL ES 3.00 generated from the WGSL by naga (internal/cmd/glslgen).

Code style: gofmt; no comments in code except terse godoc on exported API (first sentence starts with the symbol name), `//go:` and `//gpui:` directives and generated-file headers; no per-file licence headers (LICENSE + NOTICE cover it); errors wrapped with `%w`; no new third-party dependency; no `init` side effects other than registration and the platform thread lock.

Verification: a stage is finished when `sh /home/strange/Projects/gpui-go-wt/port/docs/port/verify.sh <stage>` exits 0. It runs exactly the commands in the stage's Verify block in STAGES.md (build, vet, test and gofmt on the stage's own packages, `go test -c -o /dev/null` for other targets, plus paritycheck), never a whole-repo build except in exit stages. Build outputs go to /dev/null, never /tmp. Builders do not edit verify.sh or STAGES.md; an exit stage may, changing both together.

Running things: shell commands start with `cd /home/strange/Projects/gpui-go-wt/port &&` (the working directory resets between calls). Anything that can take more than about 20 seconds (full test runs, cgo builds of render/wgpu, CI waits) runs in the background; never sleep-poll in the foreground. Run examples and spikes only through internal/cmd/shoot or with `timeout`, at low priority, and leave no window, process or headless output behind.

Screenshots: internal/cmd/shoot (built in M1-exit) is the only way examples are captured; images go to docs/port/screenshots/<group>/<example>.png. `-may-exit` accepts a program that exits 0 before a window appears; `-no-window <duration>` is for programs that never open one (success if alive at the deadline or exited 0). Open every image with the Read tool and check it for missing content, clipping, blur and wrong framing before it is recorded as verified. What cannot be checked on this machine is an owner check (decision 30); it is never claimed as verified.

Git: branch feat/port, base dev, no Co-Authored-By lines. Only the exit and CI stages commit and push, and only the paths of stages that have a docs/port/status/<stage>.done file (skip if the harness already committed them); never `git add -A`, never force-push. M0-exit opens the draft PR so the macOS and Windows runners compile the root and leaf packages from then on. Exits before M4 never commit internal/apple, internal/win, platform/apple, platform/macos, platform/ios, platform/windows, a11y/macos, a11y/windows or examples/ios_ios, even when those stages are done: the Apple and iOS paths are first committed by M4-ci-macos, the Windows paths by M4-ci-windows, so an unfinished platform never turns an earlier exit's CI red. Web stages are committed like Linux code by the first exit after they are done (the web renderer files before M1-exit, which depends on them; platform/web and the web example by M3-exit at the latest).

Scheduling: at most three stages run at once and at most one core stage at a time. When more are ready than there are free builders, take the highest Prio in the Stage index (the length of the longest dependency chain from the stage to M4-exit), ties by order in this file. The root chain is the critical path; the other lanes feed it.

Owner decisions (DESIGN 14, all decided): (1) Wayland goes through libwayland-client with purego, with typed wrappers from the in-repo generator wlgen; (2) D-Bus is github.com/godbus/dbus/v5 v5.2.4; (3) the WebGL fallback is ported (M4-web-webgl-shaders, M4-web-webgl); wgpu-native v29 against upstream's wgpu 30 is the accepted limit L-WGPUVER with a TECH_DEBT entry to bump the binding; the multi-threaded web dispatcher is the accepted limit L-WEBTHREADS and every shared path follows upstream's single-threaded branch; (4) action JSON schema comes from internal/jsonschema; (5) screen capture is ported: Linux through the xdg ScreenCast portal plus PipeWire (purego over libpipewire-0.3) and X11 capture, Windows through Windows.Graphics.Capture, macOS through ScreenCaptureKit as upstream, plus visual_test.rs. Accessibility adapters are native Go ports of accesskit_consumer / atspi / macos / windows.

Known parity limits are only L-GLYPH (Linux glyph pixels vs swash), L-JPEG (JPEG decode values), L-SVGTEXT (text and embedded images inside SVG), L-WGPUVER (wgpu-native v29 binding against upstream's wgpu 30: missing EnumerateAdapters, DUAL_SOURCE_BLENDING or TRANSIENT_ATTACHMENT use the fallbacks of M1-wgpu-context) and L-WEBTHREADS (Go wasm has no threads, so the multi-threaded web dispatcher is absent); each row using one cites the id. Licence: Apache-2.0 LICENSE plus NOTICE crediting Zed Industries (GPUI is Apache-2.0).

Owner checks: what only a person can confirm (macOS, Windows or iOS on screen, a browser, an interactive portal dialog, VoiceOver / Narrator) is written to docs/port/owner-checks/<stage>.md as `YOU: <what to check, where>`; exit and CI stages fold those files into docs/port/OWNER-CHECKS.md. An owner check never leaves a row `blocked`.
